overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Morning Service Reaches Its Climax
overview.subtitle: Tamid 33a–33b — mishnayot 5:5 through 7:4
overview.hebrewSource: וְכׇל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד בְּבֹאוֹ לְכַפֵּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ עַד צֵאתוֹ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Tamid has walked through the morning service in order, and this daf carries it to its end. Coals are moved from the outer altar to the golden pan, the shovel is hurled to signal the whole city, the lamps are tended, and the incense is offered in a Sanctuary that everyone else must leave. Then the priests descend the twelve steps and bless the people — in the Temple's own form, with one blessing, hands raised overhead, and the explicit Name. The tractate closes with the High Priest at the altar, the trumpets, ben Arza's cymbals, and the list of the psalm sung on each day of the week.

slides.title: 🔥 Moving the Coals — Silver to Gold
slides.subtitle: Mishna 5:5, and what was done on Shabbat

steps.content: 1️⃣ The priest takes the silver coal pan up the outer altar and clears the extinguished coals aside
2️⃣ He shovels four kav of consumed coals from the depths of the flame
3️⃣ He descends and empties them into the gold coal pan, which holds only three kav — so about one kav spills onto the courtyard floor
4️⃣ On a weekday the spilled coals are swept into the canal; on Shabbat, when extinguishing is forbidden, a pesakhter is overturned upon them

5️⃣ The pesakhter — a half-kor vessel with two chains, one to pull it down the ramp and one to steady it — served three purposes: covering spilled coals, covering a creeping animal's carcass found on Shabbat, and carrying ashes down from the altar

callout.label: Why gold is smaller:
callout.text: The deliberate mismatch of vessels means the transfer always spills — the mishna records the practice, and the Shabbat workaround it required, rather than treating the spill as a mishap.

slides.title: 🔔 The Shovel Thrown Between the Hall and the Altar
slides.subtitle: Mishna 5:6 — one sound, three separate messages

nodes.content: 🥄 One of the two priests hurls the shovel down between the Entrance Hall and the outer altar
📣 No one in Jerusalem could hear another person speak over the noise

columns.label: A priest hears it
columns.content: His brethren are entering to prostrate in the Sanctuary — he runs to join them

columns.label: A Levite hears it
columns.content: His brethren are taking their places on the platform to sing — he runs to sing with them

columns.label: The watch head hears it
columns.content: He stations the ritually impure priests at the eastern gate

callout.label: Function:
callout.text: A single unmistakable noise coordinates three different groups at once, without a word spoken — the Temple's public clock.

slides.title: 🕎 Inside the Sanctuary: Ash, Lamps and Incense
slides.subtitle: Mishnayot 6:1–6:3, in the order the priests entered
rows: Retrieved the basket he had left there
If both burning: clean the easternmost, leave the next one lit — the afternoon lamps are kindled from it
If the western lamp had gone out
Remove its ashes and rekindle it from the fire of the outer altar
Piled the coals on the inner altar, then flattened them with the pan's base
Handed the vessel to a friend or relative who entered with him
Scattered incense was returned to him in handfuls
Flattened it over the coals; left once the Sanctuary filled with smoke
Waited for the appointed priest's word: 'Burn the incense'

callout.label: The warning and the clearing:
callout.text: Experienced priests would caution him — 'Be careful, do not begin scattering in front of you and get burned.' And from 'there shall be no man in the Tent of Meeting… until he comes out' (Lev. 16:17), the area between the Hall and the altar was emptied. To a High Priest the appointed one said deferentially: My master, the High Priest, burn the incense.

slides.title: 🙌 The Priestly Benediction: Temple vs. Everywhere Else
slides.subtitle: Mishna 7:2 — the priests stand on the twelve stairs with five vessels

boxes.title: In the Temple
items: The people answer: 'Blessed are You Lord, God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting'

boxes.title: The High Priest's exception
items: He does not raise his hands above the frontplate, which bears God's name
Rabbi Yehuda: even he raises them above it, as Scripture says of Aaron's blessing that he lifted his hands

callout.label: The five vessels:
callout.text: Basket of inner-altar ashes, jug of Candelabrum ashes, the coal pan, the incense bowl, and the spoon — set on the ground before the blessing was recited.

slides.title: 🎺 The Libation, the Trumpets and the Psalm
slides.subtitle: Mishnayot 7:3–7:4 — the close of the tractate

steps.content: 1️⃣ The High Priest ascends the ramp with the Deputy at his right, who takes his hand at the halfway point; three priests support him when he enters the Sanctuary, and the bells on his robe signal his exit
2️⃣ The nine priests hand him the limbs in turn — head and hind leg, then the two forelegs, and so on — each slipping away after his turn
3️⃣ He circles the altar from the southeast to the northeast to the northwest, reaching the southwestern corner, where the wine is given him
4️⃣ Two priests at the table of the fats sound tekia–terua–tekia and take their places beside ben Arza at the cymbals

5️⃣ He stoops to pour; the Deputy waves the cloths; the cymbals crash; the Levites sing the day's psalm in three sections, a tekia at each break and the people prostrating themselves — Sunday Psalm 24, Monday Psalm 48, Tuesday Psalm 82

callout.label: Signalling:
callout.text: Cloths, trumpets and cymbals are all cues, not ornament: the libation, the song and the people's prostration have to be synchronised across a crowded courtyard.

summary.principle: The morning service ends as a single choreographed sequence — coals, incense, blessing, libation and psalm — coordinated entirely by sound: a hurled shovel, bells, trumpets and cymbals.

flowSteps.content: 🔥 Four kav of coals from silver pan to gold pan; a kav spills, swept away or covered with a pesakhter on Shabbat
🔔 The shovel is thrown — priests come to prostrate, Levites to sing, the impure are stationed at the eastern gate

columns.content: 🕎 Lamps tended; the western lamp kept lit to kindle the afternoon Candelabrum
🌫️ Incense burned in an emptied Sanctuary — 'no man in the Tent of Meeting… until he comes out'

flowSteps.content: 🙌 Five vessels set down on the twelve stairs; the Benediction as one blessing, hands overhead, the explicit Name
🎓 Key Principle: the High Priest pours at the southwestern corner as trumpets, cymbals and the day's psalm sound together — the daily offering completed as public worship

quiz.q: Why did approximately one kav of coals spill when they were transferred between the coal pans?
o: Because the priest was required to scatter some deliberately
Because the silver pan held four kav while the gold pan held only three
Because the coals were still burning and could not be contained
Because the ramp was steep and the pan unsteady
quiz.e: The priest shoveled four kav into the silver pan on the outer altar, but the gold pan used inside held three, so the surplus fell to the courtyard floor.

quiz.q: What were the three uses of the pesakhter?
o: Carrying incense, coals, and ashes
Covering spilled coals on Shabbat, covering a creeping animal's carcass on Shabbat, and taking ashes down from the altar
Holding water, wine, and oil for the libations
Washing the priests' hands, feet, and vessels
quiz.e: The mishna lists exactly these three. Its two chains — one to pull it down the ramp and one to steady it from above — served its standard use of removing ashes.

quiz.q: What did a Levite understand when he heard the sound of the thrown shovel?
o: That the daily offering had been slaughtered
That the High Priest was entering the Sanctuary
That his fellow Levites were taking their places on the platform to sing
That the incense had been burned
quiz.e: The single sound carried three messages at once: priests ran to prostrate themselves, Levites ran to sing, and the head of the non-priestly watch stationed the impure priests at the eastern gate.

quiz.q: How does the Priestly Benediction in the Temple differ from the Benediction recited elsewhere?
o: It is recited as one blessing with hands raised above the head, and the people respond with a formula of praise rather than amen
It is recited as three blessings with amen after each
It is recited silently
Only the High Priest may recite it
quiz.e: In the country it is three blessings with amen and hands at shoulder height; in the Temple it is one blessing, hands overhead, the explicit Name, and the response 'Blessed are You Lord, God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting'.

quiz.q: In what order did the High Priest circle the altar to reach the place of the libation?
o: Southwest directly, without circling
Southeast, northeast, northwest, then southwest
Northwest, southwest, southeast, then northeast
He did not circle; the wine was brought to him
quiz.e: Standing at the top of the ramp on the south, he proceeds southeast → northeast → northwest → southwest, and only at the southwestern corner is he given the wine to pour.
